newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway mid-curve bond sales pushes long yields up.
newsitem.headline: Norway mid-curve bond sales pushes long yields up.

text.p: 1400 GMT -- Norwegian long-term debt yields rose and underperformed Germany after negative sentiment sparked selling in the mid-section of the yield curve.
Short-term rates were mainly stable, as was the crown.
Dealers said there was selling of the government four-year bond, S466, which led market makers to hedge risk and sell the five-year segment.
"Most market makers are extremely jumpy and turnaround whatever they get as soon as possible," said one player. "The downside is more risky at the moment than the upside."

That dealer said there appeared to be "more serious profit-taking sentiment" in Norway than other Scandinavian markets following the release of higher than expected Norwegian retail sales figures for June on Wednesday.
"Those figures just fuelled fears of inflation," he said. "Maybe it (the market) is a little oversold in the short term but there is an expectation of more bad news to come. I'm negative to neutral."
* 2007 bond yield three basis points higher at 5.89 pct
* Norway over Bunds gap four basis points wider at 40 points
* Crown 102.01 vs inverse European Currency Unit index vs 102.09
